                [32m'* **Input arguments object**:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```typescript\n'[39m +
                [32m'  {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    search?: string;     // Full-text search term across name and description\n'[39m +
                [32m'    category?: string;   // Exact category match\n'[39m +
                [32m'    brand?: string;      // Exact brand match\n'[39m +
                [32m'    minPrice?: number;   // Minimum price (inclusive)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    maxPrice?: number;   // Maximum price (inclusive)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    inStock?: boolean;   // If true, only return products where inStock is true\n'[39m +
                [32m"    sortBy?: 'price_asc' | 'price_desc' | 'rating_desc' | 'createdAt_desc';\n"[39m +
                [32m'    limit?: number;      // Number of items to return (default 10)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    cursor?: number;     // Product ID cursor for pagination\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Output object**:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```typescript\n'[39m +
                [32m'  {\n'[39m +

                [32m'    };\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                [32m"* **Full-Text Search Logic**: Search must perform PostgreSQL full-text search across `name` and `description` using Prisma's `search` modifier (e.g. `name: { search: searchQuery }`), or fallback gracefully if search is empty or invalid.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* **Facet Counts Logic**: The `facets` counts must dynamically reflect the counts of products matching the *current search query and all active filters* (category, brand, price, stock).                 [32m"* **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based pagination using the product `id`. Return the `nextCursor` representing the last product's ID on the current page if there are more products, or `null` if there are no more products.\n"[39m +

Ss   15:10   0:00 bash -lc set -o pipefail; cat > /tmp/pochi_cmd.sh << \'CMD_EOF\' set -o pipefail cat <<\'EOF\' | pochi --model google/gemini-3.5-flash --max-steps 200 --max-retries 10 --blobs-dir /logs/agent/pochi/blobs --experimental-stream-trajectory /logs/agent/pochi/trajectory.jsonl --experimental-stream-trajectory-strip-duplicates > >(tee /logs/agent/pochi/stdout.txt) 2> >(tee /logs/agent/pochi/stderr.txt >&2) # Wasp Product Catalog with Full-Text Search, Multi-Faceted Filtering, and Sorting  ## Background In modern e-commerce applications, a robust product catalog search is crucial. It requires combining full-text search, multi-faceted filtering (e.g., category, brand, price, stock availability), and dynamic sorting, all while maintaining high performance using pagination and database-level aggregations.  In this task, you will build a Product Catalog web application using the **Wasp framework (^0.24.0)** with **PostgreSQL** as the database. You will implement a custom query that performs PostgreSQL full-text search via Prisma, calculates dynamic facet counts matching the current search/filter criteria, and supports cursor-based pagination.  ## Requirements  ### 1. Database Schema (`schema.prisma`) Define a `Product` entity in `schema.prisma` with the following fields: - `id`: Int @id @default(autoincrement()) - `name`: String - `description`: String - `category`: String - `brand`: String - `price`: Float - `rating`: Float - `inStock`: Boolean - `createdAt`: DateTime @default(now())  Configure your Prisma client generator to enable PostgreSQL full-text search: ```prisma generator client {   provider        = "prisma-client-js"   previewFeatures = ["fullTextSearchPostgres"] } ```  ### 2. Database Seeding Your application must seed the database with the following 6 products when initialized or started: 1. **Product 1**:    - Name: `SuperFast Wireless Charger`    - Description: `A high-speed wireless charging pad for all Qi-enabled smartphones and devices.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `29.99`    - Rating: `4.5`    - InStock: `true` 2. **Product 2**:    - Name: `UltraQuiet Blending Machine`    - Description: `Professional grade blender with sound dampening shield and 1200W motor.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `89.99`    - Rating: `4.8`    - InStock: `true` 3. **Product 3**:    - Name: `Ergonomic Office Desk Chair`    - Description: `High-back mesh chair with adjustable lumbar support and 3D armrests.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `149.99`    - Rating: `4.2`    - InStock: `false` 4. **Product 4**:    - Name: `VoltCharge Portable Power Bank`    - Description: `Compact 20000mAh external battery pack with dual USB-C fast charging.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `39.99`    - Rating: `4.6`    - InStock: `true` 5. **Product 5**:    - Name: `NutriBlend Compact Juicer`    - Description: `Centrifugal juicing machine with wide feed chute, easy to clean.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `49.99`    - Rating: `4.0`    - InStock: `true` 6. **Product 6**:    - Name: `Leather Executive Swivel Chair`    - Description: `Premium genuine leather office chair with padded armrests and tilt lock.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `249.99`    - Rating: `4.7`    - InStock: `true`  ### 3. Backend Query (`getProductsWithFilters`) Declare and implement a Wasp query named `getProductsWithFilters` that reads from the `Product` entity. - **Input arguments object**:   ```typescript   {     search?: string;     // Full-text search term across name and description     category?: string;   // Exact category match     brand?: string;      // Exact brand match     minPrice?: number;   // Minimum price (inclusive)     maxPrice?: number;   // Maximum price (inclusive)     inStock?: boolean;   // If true, only return products where inStock is true     sortBy?: \'price_asc\' | \'price_desc\' | \'rating_desc\' | \'createdAt_desc\';     limit?: number;      // Number of items to return (default 10)     cursor?: number;     // Product ID cursor for pagination   }   ``` - **Output object**:   ```typescript   {     products: Product[];     nextCursor: number | null;     facets: {       categories: { name: string; count: number }[];       brands: { name: string; count: number }[];     };   }   ``` - **Full-Text Search Logic**: Search must perform PostgreSQL full-text search across `name` and `description` using Prisma\'s `search` modifier (e.g. `name: { search: searchQuery }`), or fallback gracefully if search is empty or invalid. - **Facet Counts Logic**: The `facets` counts must dynamically reflect the counts of products matching the *current search query and all active filters* (category, brand, price, stock). For example, if a user filters by `inStock: true` and searches for `chair`, the category and brand facet counts must only count products that match both criteria (which would exclude Product 3 since it is out of stock). - **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based pagination using the product `id`. Return the `nextCursor` representing the last product\'s ID on the current page if there are more products, or `null` if there are no more products.  ### 4. Frontend UI Create a clean, responsive frontend page in React (`src/MainPage.tsx`) that uses the `getProductsWithFilters` query. The UI elements must use the following `data-testid` attributes to allow deterministic testing: - **Search input**: `data-testid="search-input"` (input element) - **Category filter**: `data-testid="category-filter"` (select element with options for categories, plus an "All" option) - **Brand filter**: `data-testid="brand-filter"` (select element with options for brands, plus an "All" option) - **Min Price input**: `data-testid="min-price-input"` (input element) - **Max Price input**: `data-testid="max-price-input"` (input element) - **In Stock checkbox**: `data-testid="instock-checkbox"` (checkbox input) - **Sort select**: `data-testid="sort-select"` (select element with options: `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `rating_desc`, `createdAt_desc`) - **Product list**: `data-testid="product-list"` (container element for the products) - **Product item**: `data-testid="product-item"` (for each product element, must have a `data-product-id` attribute containing the product\'s ID) - **Product name**: `data-testid="product-name"` (within each product item) - **Product price**: `data-testid="product-price"` (within each product item, displaying the price) - **Product rating**: `data-testid="product-rating"` (within each product item, displaying the rating) - **Product category**: `data-testid="product-category"` (within each product item) - **Product brand**: `data-testid="product-brand"` (within each product item) - **Facet categories container**: `data-testid="facet-categories"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-category-item"` and `data-category-name` attribute (e.g. `data-category-name="Electronics"`) showing the category name and its count. -                 [32m'### 3. Backend Query (`getProductsWithFilters`)\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Declare and implement a Wasp query named `getProductsWithFilters` that reads from the `Product` entity.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Input arguments object**:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```typescript\n'[39m +
                [32m'  {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    search?: string;     // Full-text search term across name and description\n'[39m +
                [32m'    category?: string;   // Exact category match\n'[39m +
                [32m'    brand?: string;      // Exact brand match\n'[39m +
                [32m'    minPrice?: number;   // Minimum price (inclusive)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    maxPrice?: number;   // Maximum price (inclusive)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    inStock?: boolean;   // If true, only return products where inStock is true\n'[39m +
                [32m"    sortBy?: 'price_asc' | 'price_desc' | 'rating_desc' | 'createdAt_desc';\n"[39m +
                [32m'    limit?: number;      // Number of items to return (default 10)\n'[39m +
                [32m'    cursor?: number;     // Product ID cursor for pagination\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Output object**:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```typescript\n'[39m +
                [32m'  {\n'[39m +
                [32m'    products: Product[];\n'[39m +
                [32m'    nextCursor: number | null;\n'[39m +
                [32m'    facets: {\n'[39m +
                [32m'      categories: { name: string; count: number }[];\n'[39m +
                [32m'      brands: { name: string; count: number }[];\n'[39m +
                [32m'    };\n'[39m +
                [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                [32m'  ```\n'[39m +
                [32m"* **Full-Text Search Logic**: Search must perform PostgreSQL full-text search across `name` and `description` using Prisma's `search` modifier (e.g. `name: { search: searchQuery }`), or fallback gracefully if search is empty or invalid.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* **Facet Counts Logic**: The `facets` counts must dynamically reflect the counts of products matching the *current search query and all active filters* (category, brand, price, stock). For example, if a user filters by `inStock: true` and searches for `chair`, the category and brand facet counts must only count products that match both criteria (which would exclude Product 3 since it is out of stock).\n'[39m +
                [32m"* **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based pagination using the product `id`. Return the `nextCursor` representing the last product's ID on the current page if there are more products, or `null` if there are no more products.\n"[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### 4. Frontend UI\n'[39m +

                [32m'* **Search input**: `data-testid="search-input"` (input element)\n'[39m +

                [32m'* **Brand filter**: `data-testid="brand-filter"` (select element with options for brands, plus an "All" option)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Min Price input**: `data-testid="min-price-input"` (input element)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Max Price input**: `data-testid="max-price-input"` (input element)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **In Stock checkbox**: `data-testid="instock-checkbox"` (checkbox input)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Sort select**: `data-testid="sort-select"` (select element with options: `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `rating_desc`, `createdAt_desc`)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product list**: `data-testid="product-list"` (container element for the products)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product item**: `data-testid="product-item"` (for each product element, must have a `data-product-id` attribute containing the product\'s ID)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product name**: `data-testid="product-name"` (within each product item)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product price**: `data-testid="product-price"` (within each product item, displaying the price)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product rating**: `data-testid="product-rating"` (within each product item, displaying the rating)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product category**: `data-testid="product-category"` (within each product item)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Product brand**: `data-testid="product-brand"` (within each product item)\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Facet categories container**: `data-testid="facet-categories"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-category-item"` and `data-category-name` attribute (e.g. `data-category-name="Electronics"`) showing the category name and its count.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Facet brands container**: `data-testid="facet-brands"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-brand-item"` and `data-brand-name` attribute (e.g. `data-brand-name="VoltCharge"`) showing the brand name and its count.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* **Load More button**: `data-testid="load-more-button"` (button to load the next page of results using cursor pagination; should only be visible/enabled if `nextCursor` is not null).\n'[39m +

It requires combining full-text search, multi-faceted filtering (e.g., category, brand, price, stock availability), and dynamic sorting, all while maintaining high performance using pagination and database-level aggregations.  In this task, you will build a Product Catalog web application using the **Wasp framework (^0.24.0)** with **PostgreSQL** as the database. You will implement a custom query that performs PostgreSQL full-text search via Prisma, calculates dynamic facet counts matching the current search/filter criteria, and supports cursor-based pagination.  ## Requirements  ### 1. Database Schema (`schema.prisma`) Define a `Product` entity in `schema.prisma` with the following fields: - `id`: Int @id @default(autoincrement()) - `name`: String - `description`: String - `category`: String - `brand`: String - `price`: Float - `rating`: Float - `inStock`: Boolean - `createdAt`: DateTime @default(now())  Configure your Prisma client generator to enable PostgreSQL full-text search: ```prisma generator client {   provider        = "prisma-client-js"   previewFeatures = ["fullTextSearchPostgres"] } ```  ### 2. Database Seeding Your application must seed the database with the following 6 products when initialized or started: 1. **Product 1**:    - Name: `SuperFast Wireless Charger`    - Description: `A high-speed wireless charging pad for all Qi-enabled smartphones and devices.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `29.99`    - Rating: `4.5`    - InStock: `true` 2. **Product 2**:    - Name: `UltraQuiet Blending Machine`    - Description: `Professional grade blender with sound dampening shield and 1200W motor.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `89.99`    - Rating: `4.8`    - InStock: `true` 3. **Product 3**:    - Name: `Ergonomic Office Desk Chair`    - Description: `High-back mesh chair with adjustable lumbar support and 3D armrests.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `149.99`    - Rating: `4.2`    - InStock: `false` 4. **Product 4**:    - Name: `VoltCharge Portable Power Bank`    - Description: `Compact 20000mAh external battery pack with dual USB-C fast charging.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `39.99`    - Rating: `4.6`    - InStock: `true` 5. **Product 5**:    - Name: `NutriBlend Compact Juicer`    - Description: `Centrifugal juicing machine with wide feed chute, easy to clean.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `49.99`    - Rating: `4.0`    - InStock: `true` 6. **Product 6**:    - Name: `Leather Executive Swivel Chair`    - Description: `Premium genuine leather office chair with padded armrests and tilt lock.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `249.99`    - Rating: `4.7`    - InStock: `true`  ### 3. Backend Query (`getProductsWithFilters`) Declare and implement a Wasp query named `getProductsWithFilters` that reads from the `Product` entity. - **Input arguments object**:   ```typescript   {     search?: string;     // Full-text search term across name and description     category?: string;   // Exact category match     brand?: string;      // Exact brand match     minPrice?: number;   // Minimum price (inclusive)     maxPrice?: number;   // Maximum price (inclusive)     inStock?: boolean;   // If true, only return products where inStock is true     sortBy?: \'price_asc\' | \'price_desc\' | \'rating_desc\' | \'createdAt_desc\';     limit?: number;      // Number of items to return (default 10)     cursor?: number;     // Product ID cursor for pagination   }   ``` - **Output object**:   ```typescript   {     products: Product[];     nextCursor: number | null;     facets: {       categories: { name: string; count: number }[];       brands: { name: string; count: number }[];     };   }   ``` - **Full-Text Search Logic**: Search must perform PostgreSQL full-text search across `name` and `description` using Prisma\'s `search` modifier (e.g. `name: { search: searchQuery }`), or fallback gracefully if search is empty or invalid. - **Facet Counts Logic**: The `facets` counts must dynamically reflect the counts of products matching the *current search query and all active filters* (category, brand, price, stock). For example, if a user filters by `inStock: true` and searches for `chair`, the category and brand facet counts must only count products that match both criteria (which would exclude Product 3 since it is out of stock). - **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based pagination using the product `id`. Return the `nextCursor` representing the last product\'s ID on the current page if there are more products, or `null` if there are no more products.  ### 4. Frontend UI Create a clean, responsive frontend page in React (`src/MainPage.tsx`) that uses the `getProductsWithFilters` query. The UI elements must use the following `data-testid` attributes to allow deterministic testing: - **Search input**: `data-testid="search-input"` (input element) - **Category filter**: `data-testid="category-filter"` (select element with options for categories, plus an "All" option) - **Brand filter**: `data-testid="brand-filter"` (select element with options for brands, plus an "All" option) - **Min Price input**: `data-testid="min-price-input"` (input element) - **Max Price input**: `data-testid="max-price-input"` (input element) - **In Stock checkbox**: `data-testid="instock-checkbox"` (checkbox input) - **Sort select**: `data-testid="sort-select"` (select element with options: `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `rating_desc`, `createdAt_desc`) - **Product list**: `data-testid="product-list"` (container element for the products) - **Product item**: `data-testid="product-item"` (for each product element, must have a `data-product-id` attribute containing the product\'s ID) - **Product name**: `data-testid="product-name"` (within each product item) - **Product price**: `data-testid="product-price"` (within each product item, displaying the price) - **Product rating**: `data-testid="product-rating"` (within each product item, displaying the rating) - **Product category**: `data-testid="product-category"` (within each product item) - **Product brand**: `data-testid="product-brand"` (within each product item) - **Facet categories container**: `data-testid="facet-categories"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-category-item"` and `data-category-name` attribute (e.g. `data-category-name="Electronics"`) showing the category name and its count. - **Facet brands container**: `data-testid="facet-brands"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-brand-item"` and `data-brand-name` attribute (e.g. `data-brand-name="VoltCharge"`) showing the brand name and its count. - **Load More button**: `data-testid="load-more-button"` (button to load the next page of results using cursor pagination; should only be visible/enabled if `nextCursor` is not null).  ## Implementation Hints - Define the schema in `schema.prisma` in the project root. - Database: A local PostgreSQL server is available and configured. You must set the database URL in the environment or `.env` file as `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/wasp_search` (or similar, depending on the test environment). - Make sure the app starts successfully and seeds the database correctly before starting the dev server.                   [32m'  const prisma = context.entities.Product;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 1. Build where clause\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const where: any = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (category && category !== "all" && category !== "All") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where.category = category;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (brand && brand !== "all" && brand !== "All") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where.brand = brand;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (typeof minPrice === "number") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where.price = { ...where.price, gte: minPrice };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (typeof maxPrice === "number") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where.price = { ...where.price, lte: maxPrice };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (inStock === true) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where.inStock = true;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // Handle full-text search\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (search && search.trim()) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const cleanSearch = search.trim();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // Format for PostgreSQL full-text search (e.g. "word1 & word2")\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const formattedSearch = cleanSearch\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      .split(/\\s+/)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      .map((word) => word.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "")) // strip special characters to avoid syntax errors\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      .filter(Boolean)\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      .join(" & ");\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if (formattedSearch) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where.OR = [\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        { name: { search: formattedSearch } },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        { description: { search: formattedSearch } },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      ];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 2. Build orderBy clause\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let orderBy: any = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (sortBy === "price_asc") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy = { price: "asc" };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else if (sortBy === "price_desc") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy = { price: "desc" };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else if (sortBy === "rating_desc") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy = { rating: "desc" };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else if (sortBy === "createdAt_desc") {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy = { createdAt: "desc" };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } else {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy = { id: "asc" };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 3. Fetch products with limit + 1 for cursor-based pagination\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const limitNum = limit || 10;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const queryOptions: any = {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    where,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    take: limitNum + 1,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    orderBy: [orderBy, { id: "asc" }],\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (cursor) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    queryOptions.cursor = { id: cursor };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    queryOptions.skip = 1;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let products = [];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  try {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    products = await prisma.findMany(queryOptions);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (error) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    console.error("Prisma search failed, falling back to contains search", error);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // Fallback to "contains" search if full-text search fails due to syntax or database reasons\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    if (search && search.trim()) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      const cleanSearch = search.trim();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where.OR = [\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        { name: { contains: cleanSearch, mode: "insensitive" } },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        { description: { contains: cleanSearch, mode: "insensitive" } },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      ];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      queryOptions.where = where;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    products = await prisma.findMany(queryOptions);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 4. Determine nextCursor\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let nextCursor: number | null = null;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  if (products.length > limitNum) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const lastProduct = products[products.length - 2]; // since we fetched limitNum + 1, the last one is the extra\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    nextCursor = lastProduct.id;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    products = products.slice(0, limitNum);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // 5. Calculate Facets\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // Group by category and brand matching the *current search query and all active filters*\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const allCategories = ["Electronics", "Home & Kitchen", "Furniture"];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const allBrands = ["VoltCharge", "NutriBlend", "ErgoComfort"];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let categoryGroups: any[] = [];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  let brandGroups: any[] = [];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  try {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    categoryGroups = await prisma.groupBy({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      by: ["category"],\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      _count: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        category: true,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    brandGroups = await prisma.groupBy({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      by: ["brand"],\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      where,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      _count: {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        brand: true,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (error) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    console.error("Facets calculation failed, falling back to manual grouping", error);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // If full-text search is active and groupBy fails, we can query all matching products and group them in JS\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const allMatchingProducts = await prisma.findMany({ where });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const catMap: Record<string, number> = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const brMap: Record<string, number> = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    for (const p of allMatchingProducts) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      catMap[p.category] = (catMap[p.category] || 0) + 1;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      brMap[p.brand] = (brMap[p.brand] || 0) + 1;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    categoryGroups = Object.entries(catMap).map(([category, count]) => ({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      category,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      _count: { category: count },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    brandGroups = Object.entries(brMap).map(([brand, count]) => ({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      brand,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      _count: { brand: count },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const categoryMap: Record<string, number> = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  for (const cat of allCategories) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    categoryMap[cat] = 0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  for (const g of categoryGroups) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    categoryMap[g.category] = g._count.category;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const categories = Object.entries(categoryMap).map(([name, count]) => ({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    name,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    count,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const brandMap: Record<string, number> = {};\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  for (const b of allBrands) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    brandMap[b] = 0;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  for (const g of brandGroups) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    brandMap[g.brand] = g._count.brand;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const brands = Object.entries(brandMap).map(([name, count]) => ({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    name,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    count,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  return {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    products,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    nextCursor,\n'[39m +

                  [32m'      categories,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      brands,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'}\n'[39m +

It requires combining full-text search, multi-faceted filtering (e.g., category, brand, price, stock availability), and dynamic sorting, all while maintaining high performance using pagination and database-level aggregations.  In this task, you will build a Product Catalog web application using the **Wasp framework (^0.24.0)** with **PostgreSQL** as the database. You will implement a custom query that performs PostgreSQL full-text search via Prisma, calculates dynamic facet counts matching the current search/filter criteria, and supports cursor-based pagination.  ## Requirements  ### 1. Database Schema (`schema.prisma`) Define a `Product` entity in `schema.prisma` with the following fields: - `id`: Int @id @default(autoincrement()) - `name`: String - `description`: String - `category`: String - `brand`: String - `price`: Float - `rating`: Float - `inStock`: Boolean - `createdAt`: DateTime @default(now())  Configure your Prisma client generator to enable PostgreSQL full-text search: ```prisma generator client {   provider        = "prisma-client-js"   previewFeatures = ["fullTextSearchPostgres"] } ```  ### 2. Database Seeding Your application must seed the database with the following 6 products when initialized or started: 1. **Product 1**:    - Name: `SuperFast Wireless Charger`    - Description: `A high-speed wireless charging pad for all Qi-enabled smartphones and devices.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `29.99`    - Rating: `4.5`    - InStock: `true` 2. **Product 2**:    - Name: `UltraQuiet Blending Machine`    - Description: `Professional grade blender with sound dampening shield and 1200W motor.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `89.99`    - Rating: `4.8`    - InStock: `true` 3. **Product 3**:    - Name: `Ergonomic Office Desk Chair`    - Description: `High-back mesh chair with adjustable lumbar support and 3D armrests.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `149.99`    - Rating: `4.2`    - InStock: `false` 4. **Product 4**:    - Name: `VoltCharge Portable Power Bank`    - Description: `Compact 20000mAh external battery pack with dual USB-C fast charging.`    - Category: `Electronics`    - Brand: `VoltCharge`    - Price: `39.99`    - Rating: `4.6`    - InStock: `true` 5. **Product 5**:    - Name: `NutriBlend Compact Juicer`    - Description: `Centrifugal juicing machine with wide feed chute, easy to clean.`    - Category: `Home & Kitchen`    - Brand: `NutriBlend`    - Price: `49.99`    - Rating: `4.0`    - InStock: `true` 6. **Product 6**:    - Name: `Leather Executive Swivel Chair`    - Description: `Premium genuine leather office chair with padded armrests and tilt lock.`    - Category: `Furniture`    - Brand: `ErgoComfort`    - Price: `249.99`    - Rating: `4.7`    - InStock: `true`  ### 3. Backend Query (`getProductsWithFilters`) Declare and implement a Wasp query named `getProductsWithFilters` that reads from the `Product` entity. - **Input arguments object**:   ```typescript   {     search?: string;     // Full-text search term across name and description     category?: string;   // Exact category match     brand?: string;      // Exact brand match     minPrice?: number;   // Minimum price (inclusive)     maxPrice?: number;   // Maximum price (inclusive)     inStock?: boolean;   // If true, only return products where inStock is true     sortBy?: \'price_asc\' | \'price_desc\' | \'rating_desc\' | \'createdAt_desc\';     limit?: number;      // Number of items to return (default 10)     cursor?: number;     // Product ID cursor for pagination   }   ``` - **Output object**:   ```typescript   {     products: Product[];     nextCursor: number | null;     facets: {       categories: { name: string; count: number }[];       brands: { name: string; count: number }[];     };   }   ``` - **Full-Text Search Logic**: Search must perform PostgreSQL full-text search across `name` and `description` using Prisma\'s `search` modifier (e.g. `name: { search: searchQuery }`), or fallback gracefully if search is empty or invalid. - **Facet Counts Logic**: The `facets` counts must dynamically reflect the counts of products matching the *current search query and all active filters* (category, brand, price, stock). For example, if a user filters by `inStock: true` and searches for `chair`, the category and brand facet counts must only count products that match both criteria (which would exclude Product 3 since it is out of stock). - **Pagination**: Implement cursor-based pagination using the product `id`. Return the `nextCursor` representing the last product\'s ID on the current page if there are more products, or `null` if there are no more products.  ### 4. Frontend UI Create a clean, responsive frontend page in React (`src/MainPage.tsx`) that uses the `getProductsWithFilters` query. The UI elements must use the following `data-testid` attributes to allow deterministic testing: - **Search input**: `data-testid="search-input"` (input element) - **Category filter**: `data-testid="category-filter"` (select element with options for categories, plus an "All" option) - **Brand filter**: `data-testid="brand-filter"` (select element with options for brands, plus an "All" option) - **Min Price input**: `data-testid="min-price-input"` (input element) - **Max Price input**: `data-testid="max-price-input"` (input element) - **In Stock checkbox**: `data-testid="instock-checkbox"` (checkbox input) - **Sort select**: `data-testid="sort-select"` (select element with options: `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `rating_desc`, `createdAt_desc`) - **Product list**: `data-testid="product-list"` (container element for the products) - **Product item**: `data-testid="product-item"` (for each product element, must have a `data-product-id` attribute containing the product\'s ID) - **Product name**: `data-testid="product-name"` (within each product item) - **Product price**: `data-testid="product-price"` (within each product item, displaying the price) - **Product rating**: `data-testid="product-rating"` (within each product item, displaying the rating) - **Product category**: `data-testid="product-category"` (within each product item) - **Product brand**: `data-testid="product-brand"` (within each product item) - **Facet categories container**: `data-testid="facet-categories"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-category-item"` and `data-category-name` attribute (e.g. `data-category-name="Electronics"`) showing the category name and its count. - **Facet brands container**: `data-testid="facet-brands"` containing elements with `data-testid="facet-brand-item"` and `data-brand-name` attribute (e.g. `data-brand-name="VoltCharge"`) showing the brand name and its count. - **Load More button**: `data-testid="load-more-button"` (button to load the next page of results using cursor pagination; should only be visible/enabled if `nextCursor` is not null).  ## Implementation Hints - You must set the database URL in the environment or `.env` file as `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/wasp_search` (or similar, depending on the test environment). - Make sure the app starts successfully and seeds the database correctly before starting the dev server.
